title: The Revelation of God's Righteousness
english: It happens that one is practicing the practical training. Therefore, it is fitting that joy and divine incense rise to those who possess the capacity for contemplation, and light to the one who achieves the goal. Regarding the things falling into this, it is said in the 945th Psalm [Ps 96:12b] to use the same word there.

The Savior has been shown through many things to be the right hand and arm of God, according to the placement of the right hand and the arm [Ps 97:1]. It is not by his right hand that God saves those being led toward blessedness. For not everyone being saved by the Lord God is saved, but rather only the one and all who, according to the right reason, are being delivered from evils and sufferings and have received the knowledge of the truth with piety. For he who is saved from diseases and wounds is not entirely saved by God, especially since he does not know if health was given to him by God, nor is he [saved by God] if he has remained unharmed from war, robbers, or such-like dangers. But the one and all who are saved from such things are saved by God, provided he does not attribute to God the cause of having suffered nothing. Since the Savior did not come to seek and save the lost [Luke 19:10] but to judge the world, he saves by God those being benefited by him, giving to them the things toward blessedness on the right hand.

And the arm of God is holy, not by participating in holiness, but as the arm of the Holy Spirit. And perhaps the right hand is called the active power of God, not being the Word of God, because it does so righteously—that is, holily, wisely, praiseworthily, and blamelessly doing all things—and the arm because of the strength and the surpassing power. As the right hand and arm of God [Ps 97:1], so also Christ is his salvation and his righteousness. Indeed, 'all flesh shall see' [Ps 98:4] intends to make manifest that all men, through being saved, shall see the salvation of God, namely Christ, the one providing the salvation. And also 'He made it known'; for he is able to say 'He revealed'...
The middle is the knowledge; of these things he is not five, but has made [them] known. For someone comes to know those things by a dim prior conception, arriving at fully knowing them.

Since it is not naturally contained in the understanding of men as God's conception—just as His Word alone is the provider of perfect virtue and the setter of the laws of nature—God sent this understanding of the Word into the visible world, having sent His own Son the Savior into the world at the end of days, so it is rightly said that God has made known His own Savior among the nations. Having made known His own Savior according to the intention of saving, God revealed also His righteousness, which is the same as the Savior, as if it were one; for it has become for us, from God, righteousness and sanctification. For these things were simply hidden from us; but when it became possible for us to approach Him, the righteousness was revealed to us.

If someone says the righteousness through the faith of Jesus Christ, and there is something proposed concerning it, he will say that this righteousness has been revealed iconically and according to a shadow, which Paul called righteousness according to the law, having ceased, clearly showing the shadow; for apart from the law the righteousness of God has been manifested (Rom 3:21), being witnessed by the law and the prophets. And it has been manifested and revealed to those among whom God made known His Savior to the nations; therefore not Jesus alone will be made a covenant in every nation, but the one fearing the Lord and working righteousness becomes acceptable to God. Thus the nations are justified by faith and not by the works of the law (Rom 4:3), according to Abraham, their faith being reckoned for righteousness.
